edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest a clinically meaningful but not extreme effect, especially in higher-risk or more exposed groups.
edges.mechanism: HPV vaccination prevents persistent infection with oncogenic viral strains, interrupting the pathway from cervical dysplasia to invasive malignancy. Because Cervical cancer is causally linked to HPV, this is one of the few prevention edges where the mechanism is direct and unusually well established.
edges.summary: HPV vaccination appears tied to lower risk of cervical cancer in adolescents and young adults mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.

evidence.notes: Association of human papillomavirus vaccination with cervical cancer screening: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
